function.name: get_weather_forecast
function.description: Retrieves the weather forecast for a specified location and date range. The forecast includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system in which to return the weather forecast data.

include_details.description: Specifies whether to include detailed forecast information such as humidity and visibility.

message.content:
Turbonomic is an AI‑driven application performance management (APM) platform that continuously monitors workloads, resources, and business goals across hybrid and multi‑cloud environments. For a global consumer goods company like Unilever, Turbonomic can help in several ways:

| What Turbonomic does | How it benefits Unilever |
|----------------------|--------------------------|
| **Real‑time workload placement** | Automatically places applications on the most cost‑effective or performance‑optimal infrastructure (public clouds, private VMs, containers, etc.) based on live telemetry. |
| **Business‑oriented optimization** | Uses business value models (e.g., revenue per transaction, customer satisfaction scores) to prioritize resource allocation, ensuring critical e‑commerce or supply‑chain apps receive priority during peak demand. |
| **Predictive capacity planning** | Forecasts future load using machine learning, allowing Unilever’s IT teams to pre‑scale resources ahead of seasonal spikes (holiday shopping, product launches). |
| **Unified policy engine** | Enforces consistent policies across all clouds—so compliance, security, and cost controls are applied uniformly, reducing manual effort. |
| **Cost transparency & chargeback** | Provides granular cost attribution down to individual services or business units, enabling Unilever to identify waste and justify spend to stakeholders. |
| **Automated remediation** | Detects performance anomalies (latency, errors) and automatically triggers corrective actions (scaling, migration, or alerting), improving uptime for mission‑critical services. |

### Difference from native cloud tools

| Feature | Turbonomic | Native Cloud APM/Observability (GCP, AWS, Azure) |
|---------|------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| **Scope** | Cross‑cloud, multi‑tenant view; sees workloads regardless of provider. | Provider‑specific; each cloud has its own monitoring stack (CloudWatch, Stackdriver, Monitor). |
| **Optimization Engine** | AI‑based decision engine that recommends or enacts changes in real time. | Mostly dashboards and alerts; automation requires custom scripts or separate services (AWS Auto Scaling, Azure Autoscale). |
| **Business Value Modeling** | Allows you to define business metrics (e.g., “$ per click”) and optimizes accordingly. | Focuses on technical KPIs (CPU, memory); business mapping is manual. |
| **Policy Management** | Centralized policy definition that applies across all clouds. | Policies are defined separately per provider; cross‑provider consistency is hard to maintain. |
| **Cost Attribution** | Detailed cost breakdown per workload, service, or business unit. | Cost Explorer provides high‑level cost views; fine‑grained attribution often needs tagging and custom reporting. |
| **Automation** | Built‑in automated remediation (e.g., move a VM to a cheaper zone if SLA allows). | Automation exists but usually via separate services (Lambda, Functions, Event Grid) and requires integration work. |
| **Learning Curve** | One UI and API for all clouds; reduces training overhead. | Multiple consoles and APIs; teams need expertise in each provider’s tooling. |

In short, Turbonomic extends beyond what native cloud observability offers by providing a unified, AI‑powered layer that translates raw telemetry into actionable, business‑aligned decisions across all of Unilever’s cloud deployments. This can reduce operational complexity, lower costs, and improve service reliability—all while keeping governance consistent across GCP, AWS, Azure, and on‑premises environments.
